text:
maria: Quick brain dump — proposing a very small "capabilities lite" manifest for runtime negotiation across hosted/dedicated/private. goal: avoid huge adapter shims while giving ops a clear signal for routing/fallbacks.

aj: +1 to small surface. what's in the lite manifest?

maria: thinking minimal flags only, examples:
- supports_streaming: bool
- kv_cache: bool
- max_seq_len: number
- quant_profile: string (optional)
- fallback_variant: string
- telemetry_tag: string (for cost/latency attribution)
- manifest_version: semver

sophia: i'd add "auth_mode" (hosted/dedicated/private) so control plane can short-circuit policy checks. also needs a bounded TTL so we can rotate capabilities without heavy rollouts.

maria: yep TTL is important. enforce short TTL for private so we re-check network-bound capabilities.

sam: how do we handle mismatch? e.g., hosted expects streaming but private node doesn't support it — fallback behavior?

maria: proposal: caller policy precedence: 1) caller requested capability (hard requirement) -> fail fast with clear error; 2) caller requested best-effort -> route to node that supports it or fall back to fallback_variant; 3) if neither available, return a typed error that the SDK can map to guidance.

aj: typed error + machine-readable metadata is key so client libs can auto-degrade (e.g., disable streaming in UI). include `supported_features` in error payload.

sophia: observability note: telemetry_tag must propagate through ingress -> adapter -> runtime traces so cost attribution and tail-latency breakdowns are accurate. ops needs sample tokens and model hash too.

maria: agree. we'll require control plane to attach: tenant_id, capability_manifest_version, node_model_hash, and sampled_prefix_token_id. these are small strings.

sam: migration plan? rolling out manifest to all host types will be a mess if adapters expect different shapes.

maria: keep manifest backward compatible; manifest_version starts at 1.0.0. adapters that don't understand manifest v1 should treat as "no capabilities advertised" and we default to conservative routing (assume minimal features). also expose a capability-discovery endpoint for probes.

ops-bot: FYI: created ticket INF-8243 to add capability_discovery endpoint and feature flag `cap_manifest_v1`.

aj: one more tradeoff — do we centralize capability decisions in control plane or push to runtime router? central avoids duplicate logic but adds latency.

maria: leaning runtime router for low-latency decisions, but control plane owns the canonical manifest and validation. runtime caches validated manifests with a short TTL.

sophia: doc ask: can someone draft minimal JSON schema and example flows (hosted->private failover) so product/SDK can test?

maria: I'll sketch a PR on the RFC repo today. label it "cap-manifest-lite". can we try a small canary: routing only for non-hard requests for 1-week?

sam: sounds safe. i'll volunteer to coordinate the canary and add unit tests for error payloads.

aj: i'll wire the telemetry propagation hooks with a toggle.

maria: sweet — thanks y'all. i'll post the draft link once created. :rocket:

sam: one last note — make sure the fallback_variant names are canonical (model_id@version) so we don't get ambiguous strings across hosted/dedicated catalogs.

maria: good call. we'll require fully qualified model references in the manifest.

aj: ok cool, will watch for the PR.

ops-bot: reminder: create runbook entry for the canary rollback threshold (error rate + latency spike).
